title: A Brief Current That Holds a Press

scenes.tts: If the Merkel cell holds the press, you might expect its own current to last. Does it?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Brief Current That Holds a Press. A Merkel cell with a recording pipette. Question on screen: does its current last?
scenes.narration: If the Merkel cell holds the press, you might expect its own current to last. Does it?

scenes.tts: In cultured Merkel cells from mouse pups, pressing evokes a tall, brief current.
scenes.visual: A current trace draws: a tall sharp peak at the start of the press. Label: cultured Merkel cells, mouse pups.
scenes.narration: In cultured Merkel cells from mouse pups, pressing evokes a tall, brief current.

scenes.tts: It inactivates within milliseconds, then settles to a small steady current.
scenes.visual: The trace falls quickly from the peak to a low, flat plateau. Past the recorded window the plateau is drawn dashed, labelled: assumed to continue. On screen: 370 pA peak; 20 pA steady; time constant 8 ms.
scenes.narration: It inactivates within milliseconds, then settles to a small steady current.

scenes.tts: The steady part is only about one twentieth of the peak.
scenes.visual: The plateau is highlighted against the peak. On screen: steady about 5.4% of peak.
scenes.narration: The steady part is only about one twentieth of the peak.

scenes.tts: So how can a mostly brief current hold a press?
scenes.visual: Split screen: the brief current trace above, the SA1 raster firing through the whole hold below. A question mark between them.
scenes.narration: So how can a mostly brief current hold a press?

scenes.tts: Compare charge, not peaks. Charge is the area under the current trace.
scenes.visual: The area under the trace is shaded in two colours: a 20 pA baseline band running continuously from the start of the press, and, above it, only the brief excess of the peak. Model: I(t) = 20 + 350 exp(-t / 8 ms) pA, a hypothetical extrapolation from group means. Label: charge = area under the current.
scenes.narration: Compare charge, not peaks. Charge is the area under the current trace.

scenes.tts: Predict. Suppose the steady part lasts through a one-second hold. Which part brings in more charge: the tall peak, or the steady part?
scenes.visual: A one-second timer appears above the shaded trace. Label: thought experiment, plateau assumed to last. Two empty bars wait: transient excess charge, steady charge.
scenes.narration: Predict. Suppose the steady part lasts through a one-second hold. Which part brings in more charge: the tall peak, or the steady part?

scenes.tts: The small steady part, by far. In this thought experiment, it carries nearly nine tenths of the charge.
scenes.visual: The timer runs. The baseline band's shaded area grows and overtakes the transient excess early on. Bars fill: transient excess about 2.8 pC, steady 20 pC; label: about 88% steady, assumed one-second plateau.
scenes.narration: The small steady part, by far. In this thought experiment, it carries nearly nine tenths of the charge.

scenes.tts: The peak's charge is all in within tens of milliseconds. A steady current keeps adding charge for as long as it flows.
scenes.visual: The peak's area stops growing almost at once; the plateau's area keeps growing to the end of the hold. On screen: crossover about 140 ms.
scenes.narration: The peak's charge is all in within tens of milliseconds. A steady current keeps adding charge for as long as it flows.

scenes.tts: Peaks mislead about holds.
scenes.visual: Text card: peaks mislead about holds.
scenes.narration: Peaks mislead about holds.

scenes.tts: But the membrane leaks, so the brief charge drains away. A steady current holds the cell depolarized while it flows.
scenes.visual: The Merkel cell drawn small beside the plateau. Label: illustrative passive linear membrane at steady state; assumed R = 1 gigaohm; an imposed constant 20 pA gives IR = 20 mV above rest. Not a Merkel-cell voltage prediction; real channel currents change with voltage.
scenes.narration: But the membrane leaks, so the brief charge drains away. A steady current holds the cell depolarized while it flows.

scenes.tts: The authors proposed that voltage-gated calcium channels amplify it. That is a proposal, not proven.
scenes.visual: Calcium channel icons on the Merkel cell, marked with a dashed outline. Label: proposed, not proven.
scenes.narration: The authors proposed that voltage-gated calcium channels amplify it. That is a proposal, not proven.

scenes.tts: There is a second clue, in the timing of the afferent's spikes.
scenes.visual: The SA1 raster returns, zoomed into the hold, with uneven gaps between ticks.
scenes.narration: There is a second clue, in the timing of the afferent's spikes.

scenes.tts: Irregularity can be measured. Divide the standard deviation of the gaps between spikes by their mean.
scenes.visual: Gaps between ticks are marked. Label: coefficient of variation = standard deviation of intervals / mean interval. 0 = a metronome.
scenes.narration: Irregularity can be measured. Divide the standard deviation of the gaps between spikes by their mean.

scenes.tts: Predict. In a noise-free integrate-and-fire model with a fixed threshold and reset, a steady current above threshold makes it fire like a metronome. What could randomly timed packets of transmitter do instead?
scenes.visual: Two empty spike trains, labelled schematic model outputs (integrate-and-fire, fixed threshold, reset): one labelled steady current above threshold, already regular; one labelled random release, blank.
scenes.narration: Predict. In a noise-free integrate-and-fire model with a fixed threshold and reset, a steady current above threshold makes it fire like a metronome. What could randomly timed packets of transmitter do instead?

scenes.tts: One possible result is irregular firing, depending on the timing and size of the packets. And light on the Merkel cells gave an irregular hold.
scenes.visual: The second train fills with uneven ticks, labelled: one possible model outcome. Beside it, the real SA1 hold under photostimulation: on screen, CV about 1.17, 12 units.
scenes.narration: One possible result is irregular firing, depending on the timing and size of the packets. And light on the Merkel cells gave an irregular hold.

scenes.tts: That is a clue, not proof. A branched ending with several spike sites could add irregularity of its own.
scenes.visual: The branched ending appears with several small spike-initiation sites marked. Label: consistent with a synapse, not proof.
scenes.narration: That is a clue, not proof. A branched ending with several spike sites could add irregularity of its own.

scenes.tts: So what crosses that synapse? That is still argued.
scenes.visual: The Merkel cell-to-ending contact, magnified, with a question mark in the gap.
scenes.narration: So what crosses that synapse? That is still argued.

scenes.tts: In mouse touch domes, the evidence points toward noradrenaline on beta two receptors. The channel it opens is unknown.
scenes.visual: One arrow across the gap labelled noradrenaline, ending on a receptor labelled beta-2. Tag: mouse touch domes.
scenes.caption: In mouse touch domes, the evidence points toward noradrenaline on β2 receptors. The channel it opens is unknown.
scenes.narration: In mouse touch domes, the evidence points toward noradrenaline on β2 receptors. The channel it opens is unknown.

scenes.tts: In rodent whiskers, fast synaptic currents were attributed to proton-gated A S I C channels instead.
scenes.visual: A second arrow labelled protons, ending on a channel labelled ASIC3. Tag: rodent whiskers. The two arrows are drawn as competing accounts.
scenes.caption: In rodent whiskers, fast synaptic currents were attributed to proton-gated ASIC channels instead.
scenes.narration: In rodent whiskers, fast synaptic currents were attributed to proton-gated ASIC channels instead.

scenes.tts: Neither account is settled, and neither is refuted.
scenes.visual: Both arrows stay, each with its preparation tag. Text: open question.
scenes.narration: Neither account is settled, and neither is refuted.

scenes.tts: Keep the idea. The ending feels the change. The Merkel cell holds the press. How it signals is still open.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the idea line, with a small question mark over the synapse.
scenes.narration: Keep the idea. The ending feels the change. The Merkel cell holds the press. How it signals is still open.
